summary: Fixture 19 requires each Phase 7 [P] worker to carry isolation: worktree and cites a run-partitioning algorithm in phase-execution.md Step 3. The reference forbids per-agent worktree isolation for Phase 7, requires declared disjoint file ownership (T001-T003 declare none, so they serialize), and now partitions through the partition-phase7-tasks helper. The fixture encodes retired behavior and nothing asserts the isolation field.
proposed_fix: Rewrite the fixture 19 prompt, README and parser fixture to the current contract: no isolation field, tasks with declared disjoint ownership, partition-phase7-tasks batches. Update the citation from Step 3 to Steps 3a-3b.

summary: The Codex side section names validate-codex-skills.sh and validate-codex-agents.sh as the structural coverage, but neither file exists anywhere in the repo (checks now live in Python validators). The README also calls this layer L7 in six places, while layer 7 in suite-manifest.json is the parity layer (layer7-parity) and this directory is layer 6.

summary: Fixture 18's prompt says AGENT_TEAMS_AVAILABLE is false when the env var is unset or Claude Code is older than 2.1.32. The reference and resolver require 2.1.178, an interactive session and passed live UAT, so the fixture states a retired capability rule.

summary: The fixture 03 sample spec says Clarify should tag the password-hashing ambiguity [codebase, domain]. The word password is a security keyword, so parse-consensus-categories widens any such item to all three analysts and raises the bar to unanimity. The unit test that guards routing skips this fixture because its prompt has no fenced tagged item. The expected.json only requires one analyst, so the drift is silent.
proposed_fix: Change the sample spec to a keyword-free ambiguity, or state that the item widens to all three and assert that in expected.json.

summary: Fixture 17 offers stop and report the blocking issue as an acceptable outcome. The reference says a blocked action falls back or defers to the end-of-run request and never stops the run or asks mid-run.
proposed_fix: Replace option (b) with defer to the end-of-run request and add must_not_include_terms for asking the user. The open stop-policy stack already does this.
